source.strategy: Kiko continues the forward sweeping stroke toward the crumb pile.
source.visibleConsequence: The bristles push across another length of rug, winding it around the broom head and trapping the front edge of the crumb pile inside the thickening roll.
source.newInformation: The crumbs are being wrapped with the rug rather than swept onto the floor.

source.strategy: Kiko lifts the broom to shake the captured crumbs onto the bare floor.
source.visibleConsequence: The previously wound rug remains wrapped around the broom head; its unwound half hangs beneath it as a broad curtain, with the remaining crumbs collected in its bottom fold.
source.newInformation: Lifting the broom lifts the dirty surface instead of separating the crumbs from it.

source.strategy: Kiko lowers the hanging rug flat and plants one foot on its far edge before pushing the broom toward it.
source.visibleConsequence: The bristles push across the flattened rug, winding another length around the head; the shrinking flat section draws Kiko's planted foot toward the roll.
source.newInformation: Pinning the rug does not preserve a sweepable surface; Kiko must step off the last exposed strip.

source.strategy: Kiko steps onto the bare floor and gives the exposed final strip one short forward sweep.
source.visibleConsequence: The bristles push across the last flat strip, winding it and the remaining crumbs around the broom head; the dirty flat rug becomes one bulky rug cylinder on the end of Kiko's broom, leaving only bare floor beneath it.
source.newInformation: The whole dirty rug has been swept up, but none of its crumbs have been swept off.
